'''Linda Sharples''' is a British statistician who is Professor of Medical Statistics at the [[London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine]]. Her research considers statistical analysis of medical interventions. She has provided expert advice to clinical trials on cardiovascular disease, diabetes and cancer.

== Early life and education ==
Sharples was trained at the [[University of Nottingham]], where she focussed on mathematics and statistics. Her doctoral research considered [[robust statistics|robust]]ness and approximation in [[multilevel model|hierarchical model]]s.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Aspects of robustness and approximation in hierarchical models|date=1988|language=English|first=Linda D|last=Sharples|oclc=1252182512 }}</ref> She joined [[Newcastle University]] as a postdoctoral fellow in 1986.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

== Research and career ==
In 1989, Sharples joined the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] Biostatistics Unit<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr Linda Sharples {{!}} Cambridge Public Health|url=https://www.cph.cam.ac.uk/staff/dr-linda-sharples|access-date=2022-01-19|website=www.cph.cam.ac.uk|archive-date=2022-01-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220119215224/https://www.cph.cam.ac.uk/staff/dr-linda-sharples|url-status=dead}}</ref> in Cambridge. She was made a programme leader in 2000.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Linda Sharples|url=https://www.lshtm.ac.uk/aboutus/people/sharples.linda|access-date=2022-01-19|website=LSHTM|language=en}}</ref> In this capacity, she developed statistical methods for assessing health technologies. The outcomes of her research were used to update experimental studies and decision models in the [[Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust]].<ref name="Professor Linda Sharples">{{Cite web|title=Professor Linda Sharples|url=http://www.anklearthritis.co.uk/professor-linda-sharples|access-date=2022-01-19|website=Ankle Arthritis {{!}} Ankle Replacement {{!}} Arthrodesis {{!}} Ankle Fusion|language=en-GB}}</ref> She applied clinical epidemiology to cardiothoracic transplants.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Methods and applications in the management of heart and lung diseases|url=https://gtr.ukri.org/projects?ref=MC_U105232027|access-date=2022-01-19|website=UKRI|archive-date=2022-01-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220119215225/https://gtr.ukri.org/projects?ref=MC_U105232027|url-status=dead}}</ref> She evaluated surgical procedure and developed multi-state models to describe the history of chronic disease.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2013-10-14|title=Linda Sharples new Director of the Comprehensive Health Research Division at Leeds Institute of Clinical Trials Research|url=https://www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk/blog/linda-sharples-new-director-of-the-comprehensive-health-research-division-at-leeds-institute-of-clinical-trials-research/|access-date=2022-01-19|website=MRC Biostatistics Unit|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In 2013, Sharples left the MRC to join the [[University of Leeds]] Clinical Trials Unit as a professor of statistics, where she oversaw the Comprehensive Health Research Division, which focussed on trials in musculoskeletal and cardiovascular medicine.<ref name="Professor Linda Sharples"/> She served on the [[Government of the United Kingdom]] Commission on Human Medicines.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Membership|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/commission-on-human-medicines/about/membership|access-date=2022-01-19|website=GOV.UK|language=en}}</ref> She moved to the [[London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine]] as a professor of Medical Statistics in 2017.<ref name=":0">{{Citation|last=LSHTM|title=Linda Sharples Inaugural Lecture: Decisions, decisions, decisions: weighing up the evidence for complex interventions|date=2018-01-30|url=https://vimeo.com/253439319|access-date=2022-01-19}}</ref> She studies how medical statistics can be used to evaluate different interventions.<ref name=":0"/> She is involved with an investigation into the care pathways of bowel cancer patients.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Improving quality of care for bowel cancer patients|url=https://www.arc-nt.nihr.ac.uk/research/projects/improving-quality-of-care-for-bowel-cancer-patients/|access-date=2022-01-19|website=ARC North Thames}}</ref>
